requests.title: Rate-limit user- and network-driven reconciliation reads to INV-04 (Rehearsal 8 DEV-R8-11)
requests.question: INV-04 allows at most four reconciliation reads in 60 s under total network failure, but SM-SAVE sends them without that bound: T-S31 (Check again) and T-S32 (back online) read without limit, and the three automatic reads (T-S19, T-S29, ReconcileDue) are not counted against any window (Rehearsal 8 DEV-R8-11; independent review RV412-1-1). How does SM-SAVE keep within INV-04?
options: A: count every reconciliation read, automatic or not, against INV-04's own window: a read is sent only while fewer than four reconciliation reads were sent in the 60 s before RequestContext.Now, one entry per reconciliation (its commit pages and file reads are not further reads), counted per investigation session. At the limit an automatic read is rescheduled (ReconcileDue) and Check again or back-online sends nothing; Check again is offered only once the automatic reads are spent. Applies exactly the transitions and contract digests listed in 'applies' under A: T-S31, T-S32 and T-S47 replaced; T-S62, T-S63 and T-S65 added; RequestContext.Now (IF41-WIRE); InvestigationSession.ReconcileReadsSentAt and the windowed ReconcileDue (IF41-SAVE)
B: amend INV-04 to count only automatic reads (a requirement change, not in v4.1.2)
C: leave the contradiction; INV04 RequestBounds stays red
requests.recommendation: A. Every path that sends a reconciliation read checks the same window, so INV-04 holds by construction; no requirement changes and the machines stay pure.
requests.rationale: Owner choices given 2026-11-02 after the round-1 review: count every read; one reconciliation attempt is one read; re-decide.
requests.impact: Until recorded, v4.1.2 cannot be compiled with these transitions (ownerRecords).

requests.title: Scope compiler: DAG covers use the full selector grammar
requests.question: tools/requirements-compiler/src/Scope.fs `covers` handles only bare requirement ids and `regex:`, while the frozen selector grammar (Model.fs `matches`: all, id:, prefix:, regex:, doc:, origin:) is what the v4.1.5 DAG uses. So T18 `prefix:PF-`, T20 `prefix:EXT-DATA-`, T25 `origin:external` and every `doc:` cover (T23) link no requirement, and the WI-GEN-* work items pick them up instead. The fix is draft PR #176 (branch claude/scope-selector-grammar, 3948d24). Under it, Rehearsal 010's approved scope compiles to 6a0e23b0... instead of 26e6ff3c..., the generated work items WI-GEN-AR, -EXT-DATA, -PF, -RECORDS, -UI and -WDL disappear (37 -> 31 work items), and the approved split plans name work items that no longer exist. How is it adopted?
options: A: (SS-1) compile and approve only the v4.1.6 competition scope with the fix, on its own digest, leaving Rehearsal 010's approved scope as history; (SS-2) retire the split plans for the competition; (SS-3) merge #176 together with the scope recompile in owner step 5
B: adopt the fix and recompile Rehearsal 010's approved scope too (its digest changes; the split plans are re-derived)
C: keep the current mapping (bare ids and regex: only); the WI-GEN-* items keep absorbing the prefix:/doc:/origin: covers
requests.recommendation: A (SS-1, SS-2, SS-3): tomorrow's scope compile must map each requirement to the DAG task that covers it, and the competition scope is approved on its own digest; Rehearsal 010's record stays as history. The owner answered "accept c" (section C of DECISIONS-FOR-TONIGHT.md: SS-1, SS-2, SS-3) on 2026-11-06 in session; that answer is not a record. This request is how it is recorded. It records only the decision; #176 is reviewed on its own and merged with the scope recompile, its tests updated to the new approved digest.
requests.rationale: It changes which work items the approved scope assigns, an owner-controlled re-scope (ScopeTests requires the committed scope manifest to equal the compile output).
requests.impact: With A, the competition scope has 31 work items and no split plan; with B, Rehearsal 010's approved scope record changes; with C, the mis-mapping stays.
